## Remote tunneling with {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Server You can securely connect to a remote machine without the requirement of SSH by installing the [{% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Server](/docs/remote/vscode-server.md) on your remote machine and accessing it through {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} for the Web (you can also connect to the server on {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Desktop). To do so: 1. Install the `code` [CLI](/download) on your remote machine. > **Note**: You can skip this step if {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Desktop is already installed on the remote machine as the `code` CLI is built into {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Desktop. 2. Create a [secure tunnel](/docs/remote/tunnels.md) with the tunnel command: `code tunnel` (you can also run `code-insiders tunnel` if you wish to use the [daily release](/insiders) of {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}) and follow the prompts to grant access to the server. This will download and start the {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Server on your remote machine and then create a tunnel to it. 3. Use the CLI's output vscode.dev URL tied to this remote machine, such as
`https://vscode.dev/tunnel//`
for access to this remote machine on any client. 4. Open a notebook file and select any Jupyter kernel or Python environment to run your code.
